prompt: Ipê's Lisbon company stores its customers' data in São Paulo. Does the GDPR apply to that processing?

choices.text: Yes; it is in the context of an establishment in the Union
choices.why: Right. The establishment brings it in, wherever the database runs.

choices.text: No; the servers are outside the Union
choices.why: No. Where the processing happens physically does not decide it.

choices.text: Only for the customers who hold the citizenship of an EU member state
choices.why: No. The GDPR protects people, not passports.

choices.text: Only after the Commission adopts an adequacy decision for Brazil
choices.why: No. Adequacy is about transfers, not about whether the GDPR applies.

prompt: A Brazilian shop with no company in the EU sells in euros and delivers to Porto. What does article 27 add?

choices.text: Nothing; the GDPR does not reach it
choices.why: No. Article 3(2) reaches it through targeting.

choices.text: A copy of the database inside the Union
choices.why: No. The GDPR asks for no local copy.

choices.text: A representative designated in the Union
choices.why: Right. Article 27, for controllers covered by article 3(2).

choices.text: Registration with every supervisory authority in Europe
choices.why: No. No such registration exists.

prompt: A Lisbon customer objects to marketing e-mails. What may Ipê weigh before stopping?

choices.text: Its legitimate interest in selling, against her rights
choices.why: No. That balancing applies to other objections, not to marketing.

choices.text: Nothing; for direct marketing the objection is absolute
choices.why: Right. No balancing test applies to direct marketing.

choices.text: Whether she consented in the past
choices.why: No. A past consent does not outweigh an objection now.

choices.text: The cost of removing her from the list
choices.why: No. Cost is not a ground.

prompt: After Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/179, what does Ipê need to send Lisbon orders to São Paulo?

choices.text: No extra transfer ground; the rest of the GDPR still applies
choices.why: Right. Data flows as within the Union, and stays protected.

choices.text: Standard contractual clauses between the two companies
choices.why: No. Adequacy is what makes them unnecessary.

choices.text: Each customer's explicit consent, collected again for every single transfer
choices.why: No. That derogation is for occasional cases, and is not needed here.

choices.text: Authorisation from the CNPD, asked for in advance, for each export
choices.why: No. No authorisation per export exists.

prompt: Ipê's analytics tool copies Lisbon orders to a region in the United States. Does the EU–Brazil adequacy cover it?

choices.text: Yes; the data passed through Brazil first
choices.why: No. Passing through Brazil does not extend Brazil's decision.

choices.text: Yes, as long as the tool is encrypted
choices.why: No. Encryption is a safeguard, not a transfer ground.

choices.text: No; that transfer needs its own ground
choices.why: Right. Each destination is a transfer of its own.

choices.text: No; transfers to the United States are forbidden
choices.why: No. They need a ground, which exists; they are not forbidden.

prompt: Within how many hours, where feasible, must a breach be notified to the supervisory authority under article 33?
A breach is known on Friday 17 April 2026 at 18:00. Why is the ANPD's deadline Thursday 23 and not Wednesday 22?

choices.text: Because the count starts on the second working day
choices.why: No. It starts on the next working day, Monday.

choices.text: Because the ANPD gives small agents double
choices.why: No. Doubled, it would be much later.

choices.text: Because Friday evening counts as Saturday
choices.why: No. Friday is the day it became known; the count starts after it.

choices.text: Tuesday 21 April is Tiradentes, a national holiday
choices.why: Right. Monday, Wednesday, Thursday.

prompt: One incident is under the GDPR and the LGPD. Which deadline does Ipê's response plan work to?

choices.text: The Brazilian one, since the database is in São Paulo
choices.why: No. Both laws apply, and the earlier deadline binds.

choices.text: The earlier of the two clocks
choices.why: Right. Here the CNPD's, three days before the ANPD's.

choices.text: The later one, so the report is complete
choices.why: No. Both laws accept a first notice that is incomplete.

choices.text: Whichever regulator asks first
choices.why: No. Neither regulator has to ask; the controller notifies.

prompt: Under article 33(4), information that is not yet known may be provided in ___.

choices.why: Article 35(3)(a).

choices.text: Large-scale processing of special categories

choices.text: Large-scale monitoring of a public area
choices.why: Article 35(3)(c).

choices.text: Sending a newsletter to existing customers

choices.text: Keeping invoices for tax law

choices.text: The name of the controller's lawyer

prompt: The residual risk in a DPIA stays high after every measure. What does article 36 require?

choices.text: Starting anyway and recording the decision
choices.why: No. A high residual risk needs the authority first.

choices.text: Asking the data subjects to consent to the risk
choices.why: No. Consent does not replace the consultation.

choices.text: Consulting the supervisory authority before processing
choices.why: Right. Prior consultation; the LGPD has no such step.

choices.text: Appointing a second DPO for that processing
choices.why: No. Nothing asks for a second DPO.

prompt: Match each system to its class under the AI Act.
Ipê buys `cv-screen` from a vendor and uses it to rank applicants. What is Ipê under the AI Act?

choices.text: The provider, since it pays for the system
choices.why: No. The provider develops it and places it on the market.

choices.text: Neither, because it is in Brazil
choices.why: No. The system is used for the Lisbon warehouse too.

choices.text: The importer, because the vendor is foreign
choices.why: No. Importer is a different role, for placing on the EU market.

choices.text: The deployer
choices.why: Right. It uses the system under its authority.

prompt: Which article of the AI Act asks that a high-risk system's training data be examined for possible biases?

choices.text: Article 5, on prohibited practices
choices.why: No. Article 5 lists what may not be done at all.

choices.text: Article 10, on data governance
choices.why: Right. Origin, preparation, representativeness, biases, gaps.

choices.text: Article 50, on transparency
choices.why: No. Article 50 is about telling people.

choices.text: Article 99, on penalties
choices.why: No. Article 99 sets fines.

prompt: Put these AI Act milestones in date order, as they stand after the Omnibus.

choices.text: The prohibitions, applying since February 2025
choices.why: Right. And the general-purpose model rules, since August 2025.

choices.text: The date of the Annex III obligations
choices.why: No. It moved them to 2 December 2027.

choices.text: The wording of the AI literacy article
choices.why: No. Article 4 now asks providers to support literacy, not ensure it.

choices.text: The date of the Annex I obligations
choices.why: No. It moved them to 2 August 2028.

prompt: Why does the page say when its dates were checked?

choices.text: The law requires every document to carry a date
choices.why: No. It is a habit, not a requirement.

choices.text: To show that this page is newer, and so more correct, than every other source on the subject
choices.why: No. Newer is not the point; checkable is.

choices.text: A schedule set by law changes by law, and a checked date tells the reader what to recheck

choices.text: Because the Omnibus requires it
choices.why: No. The Omnibus says nothing about course pages.

prompt: Why is `fraud-score` minimal risk under the AI Act?

choices.why: No. Who built it does not decide the class.

choices.text: Because it processes no personal data about any of the customers
choices.why: No. It processes orders and payments, which are personal.

choices.text: Because a person on the fraud team reviews every flag before an order is cancelled
choices.why: No. Review is a safeguard, not what decides the class.

choices.text: Annex III excludes systems used to detect financial fraud
choices.why: Right. Credit scoring is high-risk; fraud detection is carved out.

choices.text: Its obligations have applied since August 2026

choices.text: Ipê is its provider

prompt: Why does Ipê record each fraud decision with its model version, inputs, score and reviewer?
